cases.purpose: On owned loopback, rejected and accepted SSH passwords reach an inherited synthetic secret-slot device in the server and verifier child.
cases.oracle: An independently derived Argon2id KAT and project-format shadow hash, an OpenSSH password client, strict fixture host-key checking, x86-64 UAPI encoding, and exact seccomp notification traces. The synthetic peer establishes client interaction only; it cannot establish real kernel authorization.
cases.comparison: Setup separately verifies an Argon2 known vector, valid slot write/export and synthetic mint, rejects a cross-fd slot, duplicate export and invalid purpose. The server accepts only loopback connections. The OpenSSH client supplies private synthetic wrong and correct credentials through a guarded askpass helper; require rejection before mint and successful remote command after a correctly bound login mint. Record raw request/response bytes, slot transitions and client/server output. The mock acknowledges PR_SET_DUMPABLE without applying it if requested, so confidentiality is not proven. Listener bootstrap is precompiled and sends its listener before supervised operations; diagnostic stage files record the handoff. The source-review ownership and embedded-payload guard repairs are included. The CLI raw and encoded outputs and exact inputs are independently cross-checked and recorded. The owned server child is identity-checked and signaled through pidfd; supervisor and child wait/exit evidence, listener completion, cleanup signals and port closure are recorded. Forced cleanup is explicitly classified as unqualified.
